source.title: Towards Load-Aware Prefill Deflection for Disaggregated LLM Serving
source.summary: Disaggregated LLM serving runs prefill and decode on separate GPU pools to keep the two phases from interfering. In practice, this creates a new asymmetry: under bursty, heavy-tailed workloads prefill nodes saturate while decode nodes have compute underutilized, and on a production-style A100 cluster with 2 prefill and 2 decode nodes (2P2D), we find that prefill execution accounts for only 2-23% of P95 Time-to-First-Token (TTFT). Queuing and inter-node GPU-GPU KV-cache transfer account for the rest. We present a proactive prefill-deflecting scheduler that lets decode nodes serve prefill phase of requests as chunked-prefill steps interleaved with their in-flight decode batches. For each queued request, we estimate the TTFT it would see on the prefill node, and on every decode node, search for the largest chunk schedule that keeps in-flight decodes within their Time-Between-Tokens (TBT) SLO and deflect when the decode path helps tail latency. Because the prefill phase of deflected requests runs in place on the decode node, the inter-node KV transfer is eliminated. Implemented on vLLM and evaluated on production-style traces with DeepSeek-V2-Lite, our approach reduces P95 TTFT by upto 81% and raises SLO attainment by upto 79% over state-of-the-art disaggregated schedulers, at sub-millisecond per-request routing cost.

previous_facts.title: Towards Load-Aware Prefill Deflection for Disaggregated LLM Serving
previous_facts.event_hint: Kairos: a proactive prefill-deflecting scheduler for disaggregated LLM serving (on vLLM 0.18.1) that reroutes a request's prefill phase to a decode node as chunked-prefill steps interleaved with in-flight decodes, eliminating the inter-node KV transfer for deflected requests; evaluated on production-style traces with DeepSeek-V2-Lite on a 2P2D A100 cluster.
previous_facts.problem: Disaggregated LLM serving (Splitwise, DistServe, Mooncake, TetriInfer) runs prefill and decode on separate GPU pools, but under bursty, heavy-tailed workloads prefill nodes saturate and queue while decode nodes run underutilized (decode is memory-bound and leaves compute slack unused). On a production-style 2P2D A100 cluster, prefill execution accounts for only 2-23% of P95 TTFT; the remaining 77-98% is prefill queue wait and inter-node GPU-GPU KV-cache transfer. Static threshold-based deflection policies leave performance on the table.
previous_facts.mechanism: Kairos is a proactive prefill-deflecting scheduler (approx. 2000 lines of Python on vLLM 0.18.1, per-request overhead <1 ms) that lets a decode node execute a queued request's prefill phase as chunked-prefill steps interleaved with its in-flight decode batch; because the deflected request's prefill runs in place on the decode node, the inter-node KV transfer is eliminated. For each queued request Kairos computes three quantities at scheduling time: (1) expected TTFT if it stays on the prefill node given current queue depth/order, (2) time to complete the prefill phase on each decode node for a sequence of safe chunk sizes, and (3) per-decode-node TBT headroom. It then sweeps (decode node, chunk-size schedule) pairs and deflects iff both (i) TBT safety holds (adding chunked prefill does not push any in-flight decode's step latency beyond its TBT SLO, modeled analytically as a function of decode batch size, KV-cache occupancy, and added chunk size) and (ii) projected decode-node TTFT < alpha * projected prefill-node TTFT, with a single operator knob alpha>=1 (alpha=1 deflects only when strictly faster; alpha>1 allows a bounded TTFT regression for the deflected request to relieve the prefill queue, within the request's own TTFT SLO). Requires only one-time deployment-time profiling; no model changes.

evidence.claim: P95 TTFT breakdown on the 2P2D A100 cluster (DeepSeek-V2-Lite, normalized production trace): prefill execution is only 2-23% of end-to-end P95 TTFT across all five workloads; the rest is prefill queue wait + inter-node KV-cache transfer. E.g. Bursty P95 TTFT 7893.9 ms = prefill queue 840.8 + prefill exec 1070.1 + KV transfer 2175.6 + decode queue 55.6 ms; LPLD P95 6278.8 ms with KV transfer alone 4205.4 ms; HPHD KV transfer 3584.6 ms.
evidence.value: prefill exec 2-23% of P95 TTFT; KV transfer up to 4.2s P95 (LPLD), 3.5s (HPHD), 2.1s (Bursty)
evidence.baseline: measured prefill execution share within end-to-end P95 TTFT
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 5 (Table 3 P95 TTFT breakdown); PDF Page 4 (Claim 2)

evidence.claim: Complementary utilization (Table 2): across all workloads prefill SM utilization is 75-84% while decode SM utilization never exceeds 27% (LPHD peak 26.4%; HPLD as low as 7.5%); prefill HBM BW use under 1.6% of A100 2TB/s peak and decode under 1%, confirming prefill is compute-bound and decode leaves compute slack.
evidence.value: prefill SM 75-84%; decode SM <=27%; prefill BW <1.6% peak; decode BW <1% peak
evidence.condition: steady-state on 2P2D cluster, mean +/- s.d. over five workloads

evidence.claim: Chunked-prefill injection safety (Figure 1): decode step-latency increase from injecting chunked prefill stays flat (delta-Tstep <=30 ms) for chunk sizes up to 512 tokens across all workloads and batch sizes; for chi>=1024 the first-chunk delta rises to ~30 ms (low-prefill regimes) up to ~50 ms (high-prefill/bursty), so using chi>=1024 for the first chunk requires knowledge of cached prefill tokens (the regime).
evidence.value: delta-Tstep <=30 ms for chi<=512; up to ~50 ms for chi>=1024 first chunk
evidence.baseline: decode step latency without chunked-prefill injection
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V2-Lite decode batches, varying batch size and KV occupancy

evidence.claim: Headline end-to-end results: implemented on vLLM 0.18.1 and evaluated on production-derived traces (Company X), Kairos reduces P95 TTFT by up to 81% and raises SLO attainment by up to 79% over state-of-the-art disaggregated schedulers under bursty load, at sub-millisecond (<1 ms) per-request routing cost. (Reported as 'up to' maxima; the evidence pack exposes the abstract/intro claim and the <1 ms routing overhead, with detailed per-workload results referenced to the evaluation section.)
evidence.value: up to -81% P95 TTFT; up to +79% SLO attainment; <1 ms per-request scheduling overhead
evidence.condition: vLLM 0.18.1, production-derived traces, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, bursty load
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 1 (Abstract); PDF Page 2 (Contributions, vLLM implementation)

evidence.claim: Workload characterization (Table 1): five workloads derived from a normalized production trace of Company X (prompt tokens normalized to DeepSeek-V2-Lite 32K context, P25/median/P90 prompt = 2071/3569/10336, completion = 21/50/163, median P:D = 69.7), stratified into LPLD/LPHD/HPLD/HPHD with Poisson arrivals plus a long-tailed Bursty workload with Gamma inter-arrivals; NVIDIA Dynamo recommends disaggregation once P:D exceeds 8:1 (with RDMA).
evidence.value: 5 workloads; median prompt 3569, completion 50, P:D 69.7; disaggregation threshold P:D > 8:1

previous_facts.evaluation_context: Cluster: 2 prefill + 2 decode nodes (2P2D), each NVIDIA A100 80GB (compared against 1P3D and 3P1D on Bursty: 1P3D saturates the single prefill node with median prefill queue >2x 2P2D; 3P1D is decode-capacity-limited with KV-cache-occupancy transfer back-pressure). Workloads: five production-derived traces from Company X (LPLD, LPHD, HPLD, HPHD, Bursty), token counts normalized to DeepSeek-V2-Lite 32K context preserving prompt-to-completion ratio. Model: DeepSeek-V2-Lite (MoE, comparable architecture to the deployment's proprietary model). SLO targets exemplified as 4s P95 TTFT and 70ms TBT. Instrumentation: NVIDIA Nsight Systems for per-node SM/Tensor-Core/HBM-BW utilization, per-request P95 TTFT breakdown into prefill queue / prefill exec / KV transfer / decode queue. Implementation: vLLM 0.18.1, ~2000 LOC Python, per-request overhead <1 ms. Baselines: state-of-the-art disaggregated schedulers (Splitwise/DistServe/Mooncake/TetriInfer family); code released at github.com/sudokara/Kairos.
previous_facts.limitations: Headline -81% P95 TTFT / +79% SLO attainment are reported as 'up to' maxima; the visible Evidence Pack exposes the abstract/intro claim and the motivating breakdown but the detailed per-workload improvement table and the comparison baseline identity are in the evaluation section beyond the exposed evidence, so the exact conditions and the baseline for the headline ratios are not fully visible. Cluster scope is small (2P2D A100, 4 nodes) with DeepSeek-V2-Lite only; larger clusters, other models, and non-MoE architectures are not tested. The <1 ms routing overhead is per-request and does not include the one-time deployment-time profiling cost. The analytical TBT-safety model is validated indirectly via the chunk-size sweep rather than by a closed-form error analysis in the visible evidence. RDMA availability is assumed (NVIDIA Dynamo's disaggregation threshold assumes RDMA); non-RDMA transports are not addressed. The KV-transfer-elimination benefit applies only to deflected requests; non-deflected requests still incur inter-node KV transfer.
previous_facts.project_relevance: Highly relevant to the TPN card's questions: (1) Kairos is explicitly state-aware — it computes per-request expected TTFT and per-decode-node TBT headroom at scheduling time and deflects based on a TTFT/TBT condition, directly addressing whether the network/scheduler senses inference phase and KV position; (2) it targets the KV-cache cross-node transfer cost (which the breakdown shows is the dominant 77-98% remainder of P95 TTFT) by eliminating the inter-node KV transfer for deflected requests; (3) it reports end-to-end P95 TTFT and SLO attainment, not just microbenchmarks. It is a concrete answer to what scheduler-side, KV-aware deflection adds over pure GPU-memory scheduling: it exploits decode-side compute slack to remove the transfer that GPU-memory scheduling alone cannot. Caveat: the small 2P2D scale and the 'up to' headline need the full evaluation table before a deployable magnitude claim.
